# bms-connection-tester — llms.txt

> Machine-readable summary of this repository for AI assistants, code agents,
> and search indexers. Human documentation: README.md, docs/MODULES.md,
> docs/PROTOCOL.md. Full electronics build handbook:
> https://github.com/bm-a/jbd-bms-rs485-handbook

## What this is

Firmware + hardware design for an ESP32-S3 board that impersonates a
JBD / Xiaoxiang Smart BMS (battery management system) over RS485, so
compatible meters, displays, or hosts can be exercised without a real battery.
Two LEDs report link state: green = valid BMS traffic seen, red = bus silent.
v2.0 adds an 8-relay sequencer (GPIO 5/6/7/8/9/12/13/14, 12 V module, own
supply), a button (GPIO15, 3 behaviors + 10 s factory reset), a spoof trigger
(spoof trigger GPIO21 by default, configurable to safe pins), and an always-on AP web
dashboard with NVS persistence (v2.3.1: no login wall — per-request admin
password for reboot/reset/upload/OTA-admin). v2.2 adds a captive portal
(dashboard pops on join) + fixed 192.168.4.1. v2.3 adds relay count + chase wave,
2-stage spoof (100 first, then 88.8/188), per-mode ms holds, industrial pack
(loop/pause/limit, stagger, direction, labels, counters, autostart),
and manual + automatic OTA. v2.3.1 adds chase auto-sweeps, spoof trigger GPIO,
WiFi kill switch (GPIO18), and a working OTA check + Install button. v2.4 adds
a Tasmota-grade update path (exact asset match, explicit budget, image-head
gate, single finalize, named errors), per-mode relay menu (chase
break-before-make, stop dead-band, timing floors), spoof save-only, web
console, config backup/restore, custom OTA URL, one-shot STA uplink test,
info card, mDNS, keep-WiFi/bootcount resets. v1.x responder core frozen.

Also known as / search terms: JBD BMS emulator, JBD BMS simulator, Xiaoxiang
BMS tester, smart BMS responder, RS485 BMS spoof, e-rickshaw meter tester,
battery emulator for meter testing, MAX485 ESP32 BMS.

## Hardware

- MCU: ESP32-S3 DevKitC-1 (8 MB) or N16R8 (16 MB flash + 8 MB OPI PSRAM,
  PIO env `s3-n16r8`). UART2 at 9600 8N1: TX GPIO17, RX GPIO16.
- Transceiver: MAX485 / SP3485 module. DI←TX, RO→RX, DE+RE←GPIO4 (HIGH=TX, LOW=RX),
  10 kΩ pull-down on GPIO4, VCC 3.3 V, common ground, A/B twisted pair to meter.
- LEDs: green GPIO10, red GPIO11 (220 Ω to GND), driven as strict opposites,
  plus onboard WS2812 RGB on GPIO48 mirroring both (`neopixelWrite`, no extra lib).

## Protocol (JBD UART over RS485, 9600 8N1)

- Request: `DD A5 REG LEN DATA CK_HI CK_LO 77`. Read marker A5 (5A = write).
- Response: `DD REG LEN_HI LEN_LO DATA CK_HI CK_LO 77`.
- Checksum = 0x10000 − sum(covered bytes), big-endian. Requests cover REG+LEN+DATA;
  responses cover LEN_HI+LEN_LO+DATA (echoed command byte excluded).
- Answered: 0x03 basic info (byte-exact real capture), 0x04 cell voltages,
  0x05 device name. Writes/unknown registers: silence, still counted as traffic.
- Link window: adaptive 2–10 s. `STATUS?` on USB serial → `GREEN 2.4` / `RED 2.4`.

## Code map

- `src/bms_protocol.{h,cpp}` — checksum, streaming parser, dispatcher, tracker, canned frames (FROZEN since v1.x).
- `src/relay_ctrl.{h,cpp}` — sequencer (sequential/ALL-ON/chase, count, loop/pause/limit, stagger, direction, counters, chase BBM, stop dead-band), debounce, 2-stage spoof plan/builder, config (host-tested).
- `src/fw_upload.h` — update gates: explicit budget, asset match, image-head check, error vocabulary (host-tested).
- `src/ota.{h,cpp}` — OTA decision logic: version compare, asset pick, download URL, auto-check gate (host-tested, no Arduino deps).
- `src/web_ui.{h,cpp}` — always-on AP dashboard (no login wall; per-request admin password for sensitive actions), per-mode menu, NVS v3 + migration, captive portal, STA uplink + test, Tasmota-grade manual `/update` upload + OTA check/install/URL, console, backup/restore, mDNS (ESP-only).
- `src/main.cpp` — Arduino loop: frozen RS485 path + relay/web/spoof/OTA handling.
- `test/test_checksum|test_logic|test_parser|test_stress|test_relay|test_spoof|test_ota|test_upload|test_system` — 93 Unity tests (pio) + `test_web` (41, g++ host stubs) + `tools/check_web_contract.py` gate.
- `tools/virtual_meter.py` — host-side meter simulator with scenario modes.
- `wokwi/sim.yaml` — headless automation scenario (needs WOKWI_CLI_TOKEN).
- `tools/dut_emu.cpp` + `tools/raw_meter.py` + `tools/virtual_bus.sh` — PTY virtual-bus emulation (no ESP32).
- `tools/soak_sim.cpp` — 8-day continuous-run proof. `firmware/*.bin` + `firmware-n16r8/*.bin` — flash-ready.
- `arduino/` — same firmware as Arduino IDE sketch. `wokwi/` — browser simulation (relays + buttons).

## Verified facts (do not contradict without evidence)

- 103/103 tests pass (incl. original frozen 32); both S3 firmware profiles compile
  (Xtensa GCC 8.4.0); golden reply bytes verified inside firmware.bin (SHA-256 in README.md).
- Reply checksums exclude the echoed command byte (FCDA, not FCD7).
- The 188 % spoof pattern is proven on-the-wire correct (valid checksum); meters
  displaying 100 for it are clamping meter-side.
- Relay idle HIGH / ON-when-LOW = active-LOW default is bench-confirmed.
- QEMU-S3 cannot boot Arduino guests (flash-model gaps, documented); use Wokwi or hardware.
